narrative_purpose: The cold-open anchor: three Pandoran skeletons laid out together so the reader sees, beneath running legs, wings, and flippers, the same six-limbed four-eyed frame repeating - the puzzle the whole chapter solves.
subject: Three complete Pandoran skeletons laid out in a row on a dark specimen bench: a six-legged running predator (thanator-like), a winged flyer (banshee-like) with two great wing-arms and a smaller hind pair, and a six-flippered swimmer (tulkun-like). Each skeleton clearly shows six limb attachments, four eye sockets in the skull, and the lightweight bones riddled with small holes and threaded with darker carbon-like fibre.
scene: A field-laboratory bench at night, the three skeletons arranged parallel under a cold overhead lamp, the room beyond falling into dark haze.
camera: A slightly elevated three-quarter view down the row of skeletons, all three sharp, the bench surface receding into soft focus.
light: Cool clinical lamp from above plus a faint bioluminescent glow seeping from within the porous bones; deep indigo shadow pooling under the bench.
palette: Void-indigo background, cool bone-grey and pale teal on the skeletons, faint cyan glow in the marrow holes, one scarce amber pinpoint.
style: Painterly naturalist specimen plate, hand-painted texture, museum-array clarity.
detail_level: Crisp on the limb attachments, the four eye sockets, and the fenestrated carbon-threaded bone; bench and background dissolving into haze.
composition: Three skeletons as parallel horizontal bands filling the frame, aligned so the matching six-limb frame reads across all three, dark negative space above.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette with bioluminescent key from within the bone. Same dark glowing-specimen mood as the chapter cover.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no cartoon or anime style
